package main

import (
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/prometheus/prometheus/prompb"
)

func main() {
	wr := &prompb.WriteRequest{
		Timeseries: []prompb.TimeSeries{
			{
				Labels: []prompb.Label{
					{Name: "__name__", Value: "sysmon_cpu_usage_percent"},
					{Name: "instance", Value: "mon0"},
					{Name: "job", Value: "go-sysmon"},
				},
				Samples: []prompb.Sample{
					{Value: 12.5, Timestamp: 1788300000000},
					{Value: 0, Timestamp: 1788300001000},
				},
			},
			{
				Labels: []prompb.Label{
					{Name: "__name__", Value: "sysmon_disk_used_percent"},
					{Name: "device", Value: "nvme0n1"},
					{Name: "instance", Value: "mon0"},
					{Name: "job", Value: "go-sysmon"},
				},
				Samples: []prompb.Sample{
					{Value: 91.25, Timestamp: 1788300000000},
				},
			},
		},
	}
	b, err := wr.Marshal()
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Println(hex.EncodeToString(b))
}

// How write_request.golden.hex was produced.
//
// This file is .txt so the Go tool never builds it: compiling it would put
// github.com/prometheus/prometheus into go.mod, which is the dependency
// pkg/prom exists to avoid. To regenerate, copy it into an empty module as
// main.go and run:
//
//	go mod init golden && go mod tidy && go run .
//
// Recorded against github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.314.0 on 2026-09-01.
// The bytes are fixed by the remote-write v1 wire format rather than by that
// version, so a later prompb is expected to produce the same output; if it
// does not, the specification changed and pkg/prom/encode.go has to change
// with it.
